title: Deeper at constant width: 8 -> 10 layers, dim stays 512
description: DEPTH 8 -> 10 and ASPECT_RATIO 64 -> 48 so model_dim stays 512 with 4 heads of 128; pure depth change, nothing else touched.
reflection: WIN: val_bpb 0.989007 vs baseline 0.997358, -0.0084, ~9x the ~0.0009 noise floor measured in round 0. Capacity, not optimization, is the binding constraint here. The deeper model paid 24% more FLOPs/token (2.39e8 -> 2.96e8) and so saw 8% fewer tokens (381.2M vs 412.6M, 2908 steps) and still won decisively; it also ran at higher steady-state MFU (37.8% vs 33.1%) because per-step optimizer overhead amortizes over more model. Peak VRAM 27.8GB (from 22.7), 60.8M params (from 50.3). Correction to my proposal's arithmetic worth recording: vocab_size is 8192, not 32768, so lm_head is only ~4.2M params and embeddings do NOT dominate FLOPs -- depth is more expensive than I claimed and still clearly worth it. Next: push further (DEPTH 12 with ASPECT_RATIO 40, or 14 with 36) to find where the capacity/token trade turns over; VRAM headroom allows it but at some depth the token loss must bite.
